name: Balbach Teaching Dimension
definition: For $h\in\mathcal H$, set $\mathrm{BTD}^{0}(h,\mathcal H)$ to its ordinary minimum teaching-set size. Inductively, $\mathrm{BTD}^{k+1}(h,\mathcal H)$ is the minimum teaching-set size of $h$ inside the subfamily of hypotheses whose $k$th value is at least that size. Once these values stabilize, the **Balbach teaching dimension** is their maximum over $h\in\mathcal H$.
graph_summary: Iterated teaching-set dimension that filters competitors according to their previous teaching complexity.
description: An iteratively defined teaching parameter. It is monotone under subclasses, lies between recursive and ordinary teaching dimension, and is incomparable with subset teaching dimension.
origin_references: Introduced in \cite{balbach2008measuring}; its basic comparisons and subclass monotonicity are proved in \cite{zilles2011models}.

monotonic.proof: For every subclass $\mathcal C'\subseteq\mathcal C$, induction over the Balbach iterations gives $\mathrm{BTD}^k(c,\mathcal C')\leq\mathrm{BTD}^k(c,\mathcal C)$ for every $c\in\mathcal C'$. Taking the stabilized maximum proves subclass monotonicity.
